name: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Thoracic Society/Japanese Respiratory Society Consensus Criteria for LAM Diagnosis

criteria.description: Characteristic multiple thin-walled cystic lung lesions on high-resolution CT
Presence of tuberous sclerosis complex or its features
Evidence of lymphatic involvement such as chylous effusions or lymphangioleiomyomas
Elevated serum vascular endothelial growth factor-D (VEGF-D) levels
Histopathological confirmation of LAM cells in lung biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic lung lesions on HRCT plus either elevated VEGF-D levels, lymphatic involvement, or histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis can be established without biopsy if characteristic imaging and elevated VEGF-D are present.

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

occasional.symptomName: Leg swelling due to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: fluid retention in leg due to lymph obstruction
chylous fluid in chest without pneumothorax

laboratory: Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas
imaging: High-resolution CT showing diffuse, thin-walled cystic lung lesions
Chest X-ray may show hyperinflation or pneumothorax
Abdominal CT or MRI showing lymphangioleiomyomas or renal angiomyolipomas
genetic: Mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes in sporadic or TSC-associated cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating proliferation of abnormal smooth muscle-like LAM cells

distinguishingFeatures: Nodular and cystic lesions on HRCT with upper lobe predominance
Presence of Langerhans cells on biopsy
Multiple lung cysts with lower lobe predominance
Associated skin fibrofolliculomas and renal tumors
Family history of autosomal dominant inheritance

references: McCormack FX. Lymphangioleiomyomatosis: a clinical update. Chest. 2008;133(2):507-516.
Johnson SR, Cordier JF, Lazor R, et al. European Respiratory Society guidelines for the diagnosis and management of lymphangioleiomyomatosis. Eur Respir J. 2010;35(1):14-26.
Gupta N, Finlay GA, Kotloff RM, et al. Lymphangioleiomyomatosis: clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2017;196(10):1210-1219.
